title: Efficacy of Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccines Compared with Original Boosters
what_it_is: Efficacy of Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccines Compared with Original Boosters

sections.label: Bivalent COVID-19 vaccines rollout
sections.summary: Bivalent Moderna/Spikevax started 14 October 2022, Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty expected by year end, prioritising those aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I thought it would be useful to answer them and take some supplementary questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have started using the bivalent Moderna/Spikevax vaccine on 14 October 2022, and there is another bivalent vaccine – the Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty – which is expected to be available by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Bivalent vaccines provide better protection against newer COVID-19 variants compared to the original vaccines and we recommend individuals who are eligible to take it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are prioritising persons aged 50 and above for the additional booster dose with the bivalent vaccine as they are at higher risk of severe disease from infection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And I hope we will secure them in a matter of weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Those who are eligible and have recently recovered from a COVID-19 infection are recommended to receive the bivalent vaccine three months after the infection.

sections.label: Vaccination access points
sections.summary: 11 JTVCs and VCs, 221 participating Public Health Preparedness Clinics and 20 polyclinics provide sufficient access to vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Currently, we have 11 JTVCs and VCs and, together with our network of 221 participating Public Health Preparedness Clinics and 20 polyclinics, they provide sufficient convenience and access to vaccinations.

sections.label: Booster timing recommendations
sections.summary: Bivalent vaccine recommended five months after second booster, with minimum protection of three mRNA doses and boosters every five to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The answer is yes, five months after their second booster, they are recommended to take their bivalent vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I had explained earlier, we have moved to a new system where we have stopped counting the number of booster shots we take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, what we are recommending now is: one, please attain your minimum protection, which is, three doses of an mRNA vaccine; and two, beyond that, take an additional latest vaccine five months after your last shot and no longer than 12 months – so, five to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Essentially, for most people, it works out to taking a booster shot every year.
